Black Friday Is Here: Is This the Best Time To Finally Get Yourself That Budget E-Bike?
24 photos
Photo: Himiway Electric Bike
While most people are out looking for new TVs, laptops, and digital cameras, during Black Friday, I’m out here hunting down the best deals we can get our hands on. Well, here’s to e-biking and getting you mounted on a fresh budget and electrified steed ASAP.
With countless brands gearing up for Black Friday, I’ve decide to bring to light some of the brands that you should to have on your radar if you’re looking for an e-bike, be it for you or a loved one. While I’m only shedding light on just five of them, clearly, there are countless others that are also slashing prices, so take this list as a bit of a starting point, if you don’t already have one.
Engwe First up on our list of budget e-bike brands that are really unleashing all they have in terms of Black Friday goodness is none other than Engwe , the one and the same that sells all over the world. That said, the deals you can find from this crew do differ on where you are in the world.
Photo: Engwe For Europeans, one of the hottest deal that Engwe has in store is their Zip. It’s a folding e-bike that was designed to compete with Brompton, but at a fraction of the price. It was selling for €1,100 and is now up for grabs at a flat €1,000 ($1,100). If you’re wondering if you should pull the trigger on this one, keep in mind that 94 reviews have been left on the manufacturer’s website, amounting to a 5/5-star rating.
If you’re in the US, on the other hand, you can tap into the Eagle model, this brand’s electric pit bike, or pocket dirt bike. This model was selling for $1,200, but for Black Friday, this one’s flying off the shelf for a solid $800 (€750). A steal folks!
Other models are also under fire for Black Friday, actually, just about the entire Engwe lineup, marking it as the perfect time to pull the trigger on one of their e-bikes if you’ve been eyeing them.
Heybike Up next on our list of e-bike brands that are letting go of their monsters for less then ever, we have Heybike, a brand that has been on the market for quite some years, and while their e-bikes aren’t seeing massive price cuts on the same level as Engwe, they too have some considerable deals.
Photo: Heybike One important deal is the Ranger 3.0 Pro, going for $1,400 instead of $1,500, or the Mars 3.0, dropped from $1,200 to just $1,000. Again, not some massive price cuts, but Heybike already offers some decent deals, so going any lower is a bit tough.
Keep in mind that some of their dirt bikes are on sale, in particular the V1 and all it’s bundle deals and kits. The V1 Pro, however, is still going for its full price of $2,100 but does have the occasional price cut, so keep your eyes peeled for that one.
JaisonBike The name JasionBike is about as prolific as Engwe, and can be spotted selling all over the world too. Considering this crew has been on the market for ages too, they’re also able to really slash prices on their e-bikes.
One of their best deals is for their Hunter Pro, a fat tire ride going for just $960, down from $2,000. That’s over 50% off, and a clear budget ride to land on your e-bike radar. They’re X-Hunter is also a hot deal, dropped to just $880 from $1,900.
Photo: Jasionbike But, these two bikes are not alone. As mentioned, Jaison really went all out here, with rides like the Thunder Pro ST going for $1,200 from $1,900, and their Kago, a cargo e-bike, is at $800, down from $2,200, quite possibly, the best deal on their site, currently.
Duotts If there’s one brand that I noticed competing with some of the established giants on the market, it’s Duotts. This team came out of nowhere, with some rather questionable rides at first, but in time, turned into a serious crew to consider for a new e-bike.
In their lineup, the F26 and it’s Lite counterpart are a couple of deals worth considering. The standard F26 is selling under Black Friday for €1,250 ($1,380), down from €1,700. The Lite, on the other hand, is set for €1,050 ($1,150).
Photo: Duotts Just keep in mind that Duotts has really exploded in recent years, and even their more meaningful machines are seeing price cuts. One model in particular is the collab they did with 79Bike. The Falcon Pro is that model, but it’s a dirt bike, not pedal-powered, and it’s going for €380 less than before. It’s still a sizable price of €4,320 ($4,750) though, so don’t get too excited.
Himiway Last but not least, on this short list of budget e-bike names you need to be aware of, we have Himiway . One of the best deals this team has in store here is their A7 Pro Commuter. The bike normally goes for $2,900, but Himiway is letting it fly for just $2,000, and if I may, people who have ridden this bike call it the Rolls Royce of budget urban e-bikes, mainly because of the ultra-plush full-suspension and a mid-mounted motor.
Photo: Himiway Another massive deal Himiway has in store is the D7 full-suspension MTB with its peak range of 80 miles on a full charge, selling for just $2,000, down from a flat $3,000, so a 33% discount. The entire Himiway lineup has something to look for, so do so, and before the sale is gone.
While these are not all the budget e-bike brands the market currently has to offer, they are the ones that come to mind, mainly because our team has tested some of them and we have knowledge as to what they offer. Be sure to cross-read our reviews of some of the brands we mentioned here today. Until next time; wear a helmet when riding and obey local road laws.
